description: Analog partition testbenches: every committed SPICE deck behind a recorded analog measurement, every committed `klt sim` request that drives one, and the solve procedure's own Python bench (`sim/solve/`), which post-processes those surfaces into the rows 1-4 estimate and the item-6 yield figures without re-simulating. The solve bench does not stand alone: `sim/solve/solve.py` imports `sim/sensitivity/analyze.py` (for OSCS/BASELINE/PROCESS/VDD/TEMP and the sigma_quant quantization term) and `sim/solve/gen_binding_mc.py` imports `sim/sensitivity/gen_requests.py`, and `analyze.py extract` / `extract-mc` is the first step of the reproduce chain for every cited row in sim/solve/records/ and sim/solve/mc/RECORD-*.md, so those two modules and `sim/sensitivity/test_analyze.py` are inventoried here as part of that measurement path rather than left as unpinned helpers. The PEX grader `sim/pex/grade_pex.py` is inventoried on the same post-processor rationale, for the item-8 evidence chain: it turns the committed `klt pex` reports into `sim/pex/records/*grade-extracted-values*.json`, the derived grade that `characterization/analog.md` cites for the row-1 and row-2 post-layout statements and that `evidence/item8_analog.json`'s method names for the spec-row-9 analog share, so an unpinned grader could silently stop reproducing that record (issue #267). It is pinned by hash only, with no cold start of its own (like `sim/sensitivity/analyze.py`): regrading the recorded rows is the documented four-report `python3 -I sim/pex/grade_pex.py` invocation in README.md and sim/pex/README.md, which this attestation does not run, and no `7.analog` citation names the grade record itself -- the item-7 verdict cites the `klt pex` reports, not the derived grade. Cold starts are bounded by construction and do NOT re-run the multi-hour batch-fleet grids: the oscillator-bank and smoke decks run their real single-corner `ngspice -b` locally (--no-record, so a repeat appends nothing to the append-only records), the `sim/solve/` unittest suites run for real (they are pure post-processing on committed inputs), and every `klt sim` request is validated with `--dry-run` (deck staging, model resolution, corner/Monte-Carlo expansion against the pinned PDK) rather than simulated. The full fleet invocation for each grid is documented in that bench's README or `RECORD-*.md` and in manifests/README.md; it is not executed by this attestation. Being inventoried means the file is pinned by content hash and its declared cold start exited 0 -- not that a fleet run of it was recorded: 20 of the 140 `sim/solve/mc/requests-sized/` requests (the tt/1.62V/-40C chunks) are committed, drift-checked and never run, as sim/solve/mc/RECORD-2026-11-06-item6-sized-partial.md states. What each cold start does and does not cover is tabulated in manifests/README.md, "Item 9 (testbenches shipped)".
